about: 200 original bomber names and nose art paintings for the battle scenes. Brian, 20 November 2026: 'have some bomber nose art on the b-17s', then 'make 100 bomber names and nose art so its not always the same ones each mission' and 'lets actually make it 200'. Names and pictures are our own: no real aircraft's name, no real person, no real company, no character from a film, a book, a comic or a game. Numbers 1 to 24 were checked by the historian and ruled by the art director on 20 November; 25 to 200 were added the same day: the art director passed them at 16:26Z with the changes in 'rules', and the historian checked the names at 16:28Z (historian/bomber-names-200-check.md): two names changed (19, 97), and eight names of fight and swagger, the record's other big strand, took the place of eight porch and tall-tale names in batches 3 and 4 (107, 108, 119, 142, 164, 165, 171, 179). Those eight still want the historian's and the art director's eye.
side: left side of the nose, below and behind the navigator's windows, ahead of the cockpit

kinds.figure: a person, fully dressed in the clothes of the time
kinds.creature: an animal or a made-up beast
kinds.emblem: an object or a small scene with no person: the quickest to paint

batches.note: Paint in this order. Each batch mixes the themes and the kinds. The scene draws only from entries whose painting exists, so a build never waits for all 200.

rules.from: The art director, 20 November 2026 16:26Z (art-director/battles/nose-art-200-ruling.md), on top of section G3 of air-fates-look.md.
rules.read: One bold silhouette with one idea: at most three shapes, one of them clearly the biggest. No rows, crowds or many small things.
rules.words: No words inside a picture. The name is the only text.
rules.tone: No painting shows an aircraft burning, falling or crashing, or a crew in danger. Cartoon bombs aimed at no one are true to the period and stay. Fight and swagger are aimed at no one: no enemy's figure, flag, leader or slogan in any picture or name.
rules.people: Every person fully dressed in the clothes of the time. No caricature of any people or nation; where a cartoon figure of the time slid into one, paint an emblem with no figure.
rules.lettering: It must read under the battle grade, which greys paint: white, cream and yellow read on olive drab; red, orange, pale blue and light green always carry a white or yellow edge or shadow. A name over about 16 letters is block, stencil or two lines, never script. Letters 20 to 30 cm tall.
rules.review: Each painting batch goes to the art director as a sheet: every painting at nose-art size on an olive drab panel under the battle grade, plus five on the B-17 at the close view's distance. One mend round per batch.
rules.looks: Where an entry has a 'note', it names a famous look of the time to keep off. Paint from life, not from any cartoon.
rules.numbers: A number never changes hands for good: the game's records keep a bomber by its number, so a renamed entry keeps its number and a new entry takes a new one.

keepOff.why: Real aircraft. 'names' and 'serials' are the famous ones (the historian). 'alsoReal' are other real aircraft names the air thread recalls from the bomb groups' records. Never add any of them, and never paint these serials on a fin.
alsoReal: Nine Little Yanks and a Jerk
keepOff.neverUse: A real company's name or mark, a real person's name, or a character from a film, a book, a comic strip or a game. Number 11 was 'Gremlin Gus' until 16:20Z on 20 November; that is a character from a 1943 film studio's storybook and from a later video game, so it became 'Gremlin Trouble' with the same picture. Number 19 was 'Union Pacific Pearl' (a real railroad), then 'Overland Pearl' (a car marque and that railroad's train) until 16:40Z; it is 'Highball Pearl', railroad slang for the go signal.

assign: Shuffle the entries whose painting exists once for each bomber group from the battle's seed and the group's id, so every mission draws a different set of the 200. Give the group's aircraft entries in slot order: no two aircraft of a group share one until the list runs out, and two groups in the same battle may not share one either while unused entries remain. With chance 'none' an aircraft has no name: a new replacement. An aircraft keeps its entry for the whole battle; a loss never reshuffles the rest.
